subject: Q4 runway playbook — GPU runway, batching & procurement timeline
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@hannahltd.com, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Q4 runway playbook — GPU runway, batching & procurement timeline

Team — kicking off a short thread to consolidate QBR asks from leadership and procurement for the Hannah Ltd expansion. Goal: a one-page playbook we can hand to Sales + Procurement by EOD Monday (Oct 4). Topline bullets I need from owners: 

- Vivek: updated GPU runway model (per-region, monthly granularity) with current reserved + burst assumptions. See attached modeling workbook.
- Aditya: updated token-level unit economics showing effect of 2 batching/caching profiles (conservative vs aggressive).
- Lauren: leadership summary (1x slide) with the risk ladder and approval asks.

Attachments: q4_gpu_runway_modeling.xlsx (workbook), batching-cache-simulations.pdf (sim outputs)

Quick asks: can you confirm by EOD tomorrow: the runway delta if we enable aggressive caching (prefix cache on 30% of traffic) and if we commit 3 months of Dedicated capacity for the account. I want both cost delta and expected p95 latency change.

Thanks — Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-02T13:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Q4 runway playbook — GPU runway, batching & procurement timeline

Sergio — sending a quick read. Two clarifying items before I draft the slide: 

1) On utilization: are we modeling steady-state utilization at 65% or 80% for Dedicated? That pivot changes the recommended commit size.
2) On caching: when you say "prefix cache on 30% of traffic" do you mean prefix reuse (user session-level) or short completion reuse (across sessions)? Please confirm.

I'll pull a one-slide risk ladder once I have Vivek's runway numbers and Aditya's econ deltas.

— Lauren
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-03T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Q4 runway playbook — GPU runway, batching & procurement timeline

Lauren / Sergio — uploaded a baseline tab in the workbook (attached) with the currently committed GPUs by region and the 3-month consumption forecast. Assumptions included:

- Baseline utilization = 70% across committed pools (conservative headroom).
- Burst headroom (on-demand) available for +20% peak for the account for the trial month.
- Aggressive caching profile assumptions: prefix reuse = 28% hit rate, average token reduction per hit = 40%.

Topline numbers (short):
- If we toggle aggressive caching: expected unit cost/token reduction ~26% and p95 latency improves by ~70–120ms (depends on model/seq).
- If Hannah commits to 3 months of Dedicated at 40% higher base than current trial: our monthly committed spend increases by ~38% but effective cost per useful token drops ~18% (because reserved pricing + higher utilization).

I've left comments in q4_gpu_runway_modeling.xlsx; Aditya, can you validate the econ worksheet where batching multipliers are applied?

Attachments: q4_gpu_runway_modeling.xlsx

— Vivek
Director, Infrastructure Economics

From: Procurement Hannah Ltd <procurement@hannahltd.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-03T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Q4 runway playbook — GPU runway, batching & procurement timeline

Hi Sergio / Lauren — thanks for the clear ask. Procurement timeline notes from our side: 

- We can sign a 3-month Dedicated commit by Oct 18 if SLAs and SOC2 evidence are finalized.
- Can you confirm whether aggressive caching implies any additional data retention or PII exposure? Our security team flagged caching patterns in prior vendors.
- Also please share the procurement-sla-draft.docx for internal review (redlines expected).

We'd like a one-pager that includes cost delta vs on-demand, expected latency improvements, and the exit terms if usage drops < 50% of committed baseline.

Regards,
Maya Singh
Head of Procurement, Hannah Ltd
Attachments requested: procurement-sla-draft.docx

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Procurement Hannah Ltd <procurement@hannahltd.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-04T16:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Q4 runway playbook — GPU runway, batching & procurement timeline

Maya — thanks for the timeline and the ask. Quick responses and actions: 

- Data/PII: aggressive caching as we model it is at the prefix/KV level for *non-personal* session prefixes. It does not persist raw user inputs to durable storage beyond the cache TTL. Security will produce a short note; I asked Security to confirm by EOD Friday.
- SLA draft: attached (procurement-sla-draft.docx) — this is the internal draft with standard Redwood enterprise SLAs and a proposed 30-day partial-exit clause if usage drops below 50% of committed baseline.
- Action owners: Vivek will finalize the committed vs on-demand cost table (sheet: committed_vs_on_demand), Aditya will finalize the batching/caching econ deltas slide (file: batching-cache-simulations.pdf). Lauren will craft the leadership slide for the QBR.

Deliverables due: Monday Oct 6, 10:00 PT — consolidated one-page playbook + 1-slide leadership summary + procurement packet for Hannah.

Attachments: procurement-sla-draft.docx, q4_gpu_runway_modeling.xlsx, batching-cache-simulations.pdf

Thanks,
Sergio
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
